plan: Since this is the only round, maximizing profit involves winning the bid at a cost lower than my value. Assuming Betty and Charles bid close to their values, bidding slightly above the midpoint ($24.5) ensures a competitive bid. To maximize profit, I'll bid $25. This gives room to win if they bid lower, while still allowing a profit margin if I win.

Given my value of $6, I should bid low to avoid overpaying. Since the value range is $0-$49, I expect others to bid closer to their values. If I bid $5, I might win if others bid lower, but if not, I lose nothing. This strategy maximizes my profit potential without risking a loss.

Given my value of $17, I aim to bid low enough to ensure profit if I win but high enough to outbid others. I anticipate others to bid around their values. If I bid $10, I may win if others bid below $10, paying the third-highest bid and ensuring profit. If both bid above $10, I lose but incur no cost. This strategy balances risk and potential profit.
